hints.title: Suffix Dominance
hints.text: The lexicographically largest substring must always be a suffix of the original string.

hints.title: Candidate Index Comparison
hints.text: Maintain two candidate starting indices i and j, along with offset k to compare characters s[i + k] and s[j + k].

hints.title: Leapfrog Pointer Shift
hints.text: When s[i + k] < s[j + k], candidate i can be discarded and advanced to max(i + k + 1, j). When s[i + k] > s[j + k], advance j by k + 1.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Comparing all suffixes naively takes quadratic O(N^2) time on repetitive strings like aaaaaa...b.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Dual pointer leapfrog shifts skip repetitive characters in guaranteed linear time and constant auxiliary memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that any prefix of a suffix is smaller than the full suffix, reducing the problem to finding the max suffix in O(N) time.
complexity.notes: Returns the substring starting at index i through end of string.
